thresholds.deorbit_start: 75% (dynamic — adjusted lower if agents in flight)

dynamic_adjustments.agent_shift: Each in-flight agent shifts deorbit DOWN 5% (e.g., 2 agents: 70% deorbit trigger)
dynamic_adjustments.burn_shift: If burn >5000 tok/s: deorbit -10%; if >2000 tok/s: deorbit -5%
dynamic_adjustments.queue_shift: If queue >5 tasks: deorbit +5% (allow staying in orbit longer)

compact_calibration.meaning: Claude underestimates context by ~17% on average
compact_calibration.pattern: Auto-compact fires 13-30% earlier than Claude estimates. Heavy sessions (agents + large reads) have highest skew.

compact_dead_time.reality: Claude CLI handles compaction entirely in the background — the conversation summary IS the context after compact. No agent re-launch, no state loss IF piston-checkpoint.json is current.
compact_dead_time.risk: If compact fires MID-WAVE (between W1 return and W2 launch), the checkpoint must capture which agents returned vs in-flight. Current piston-checkpoint.json shows agents_returned + agents_in_flight — this IS the recovery state.

current_state.resume_instruction: Wave 3 in flight. Crystallize deep results + queue new cycle.

recovery_protocol.step_2: Check agents_in_flight — these need return handling when they finish
recovery_protocol.step_3: Check agents_returned — these results already exist on disk, do NOT re-spawn
recovery_protocol.step_4: Read surfacing_scheduler.py resume to get plan for next wave
recovery_protocol.step_5: Launch next wave immediately — do NOT re-read files already summarized

what_is_lost: Raw agent return text (compressed into summary — only manifest paths survive)
Precise timing of returns that happened before compact
In-progress agent reasoning that hadn't been written to disk yet
checkpoint_recovery_post_compact.critical_gap: W3 agents that were IN FLIGHT when compact fires will still complete — but their returns arrive into a compacted context. If the piston checkpoint correctly lists them as in-flight, faerie knows to expect them. If the checkpoint is stale (not written before compact), faerie loses track and may re-spawn duplicates.

spawn_latency.bottleneck: not spawn — it is agent execution time
spawn_latency.note: The surfacing-log has no sub-second precision; spawn overhead is below the measurement floor

recommendations: BOTTLENECK: research-analyst (avg 35min, 64% near-compact rate) is the single biggest latency threat. Consider splitting research tasks into smaller chunks that fit in a single wave slot, or route to faster specialist agents when possible.

BOTTLENECK: W1+W2 are fully serial from the user perspective. Total user-visible delay before first response = W0 (~5s) + W1 (~400s) + W2 (~500s) = 15-20 minutes typical. This is the correct trade-off for a rich dashboard, but users should know what they are waiting for.

OPTIMIZATION: Launch W1 minimum 2 agents in parallel always. Single-agent W1 waves (as observed in this session's wave1-spiderfoot) waste the parallelism window and don't reduce user wait time versus a 2-agent wave.

RISK: Context underestimation by 17% (correction_factor=1.1712) means W3 agents launched at 60% actual are effectively launched at ~70% effective. Two simultaneous W3 returns (+12.5% each) could push a 75% session to 100% and fire compact before the returns are synthesized. Monitor effective_pct in context-phase.json, not raw_pct.

RISK: Vault write permission gaps (wave2-fullstack partial completion) are silent — the manifest shows phase4_vault_readme=partial but no alert fires. Add a post-wave validation step that checks expected outputs exist before writing checkpoint.status=complete.

SAFETY: piston-checkpoint.json agents_in_flight list is the recovery anchor post-compact. It MUST be written before any W3 background spawn, not after. Current checkpoint shows correct state but the write ordering should be enforced by code, not convention.

OPPORTUNITY: context_phase.py already implements dynamic threshold adjustment (agent_shift, burn_shift, queue_shift). This is sophisticated. The weak link is the 17% underestimation bias in raw context reporting — the thresholds are well-designed but operating on slightly wrong inputs.

OPPORTUNITY: Opus 1M context (if switched) would change the math entirely: deorbit threshold rises to 85% (+10%), rounds_remaining jumps from 1 to ~8+, enabling 3-4x more work per session without compact risk. Current Sonnet 200K is the binding constraint.
